claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To get started, could you please tell me the name(s) of the child or children you'd like me to assess eligibility for?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I'd like to find out if I can claim Child Benefit. I have one child - Alex, who's 15 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! I have a good starting point now.

To properly assess Alex's eligibility for Child Benefit, I need to gather a bit more information about your circumstances.

Are you currently living in the UK, and what is your residency status (for example, are you a British citizen, EU citizen, or do you have settled status)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK - we're in Manchester. I'm a British citizen.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that. That's helpful information.

Now, regarding Alex - is Alex currently in full-time education or training, or are they working?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex isn't working or in any training. They're just at school - you know, regular secondary school for their age.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. That's useful to know.

One more important question: are you currently receiving Child Benefit for Alex, or would this be a new claim?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: This would be a new claim - I'm not currently getting Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I have one final question to complete my assessment.

Are there any circumstances that would prevent you from claiming, such as:
- You or a partner receiving certain high-level benefits (like Income Support, income-based Jobseeker's Allowance, income-related Employment and Support Allowance, or Pension Credit)?
- Or any other factors you think might affect your eligibility?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nothing like that. We're not receiving any of those benefits you mentioned. Is there anything else you need to know?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing all that information. I believe I have everything I need to make an assessment.

Let me review the details:
- Alex is 15 years old
- Alex is in full-time secondary education
- You're a British citizen living in the UK
- This would be a new claim
- You're not receiving any of the high-level benefits that would prevent a claim

Based on the Child Benefit eligibility rules, Alex qualifies as they are under 16 and in full-time education. There are no factors present that would prevent your claim.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great news! **You are eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex.**

Alex meets the eligibility requirements as they are:
- Under 16 years old
- In full-time secondary education

Combined with your status as a British citizen resident in the UK with no conflicting benefit entitlements, you should be able to proceed with your claim.

If you'd like to make a claim, you can do so through the official government channels. Is there anything else I can help you with?
